design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER — employer_quarterly_contributions task 0 (root: taxacct_ext_credit_refund_request; prerequisite: taxacct_ext_estimated_assessment).

[Step 0 — draw and scope] draw_counts.py --task 0 printed {"prerequisite_problems": 1, "problems": 2, "factor_counts": [4, 4]}; --tasks 2 printed task 1 = {"prerequisite_problems": 1, "factor_counts": [6, 6]}. Task 0 therefore has one prerequisite problem and both computations carry 4 factors (estimate 4: 3 parameter + 1 method; refund 4: 3 parameter + 1 method). Occupied before this task: nothing (task 0 is first). Claimed here: the estimated assessment write (book_estimated_assessment_54fbfb5a, owner agent, event taxacct_contribution_assessed with basis estimated_assessment) and the employer's credit refund request (request_credit_refund_f44db5b5, owner user, constraining taxacct_refund_issued). Left for task 1 (6/6): the late report penalty write (taxacct_penalty_assessed) and the employer's penalty relief request (constraining taxacct_credit_adjusted / penalty_abated) — a disjoint pair with its own natural six-factor penalty ladder and a relief schedule; no policy or tool of this task is reused there. Base capabilities deliberately left unclaimed by both tasks: voluntary contribution, revised rate notice, reserve credit, delinquency cure (their computations cannot be expressed without recomputing the computation-date reserve, and the cure carries no computed figure).

[Design thesis] Surface goal (customer, layperson): "we won our rate appeal; refund the credit sitting on our account". Core scored figure: requested_amount on the refund request. Hidden chain: the refund policy's prerequisite sentence says the refundable amount is worked out only after the ledger carries an estimated assessment for every quarter whose report is still unfiled at least the estimated assessment days (60) after its due date; the reports list shows 2026-Q2 (due 2026-07-31) has no report and the ledger has no estimate for it → the agent must first book that estimate (its own 4-factor computation), which both lowers the credit (balance_due -3,076.50 -> -769.44) and switches on the refund's estimate hold. Depth: 2 hops (refund -> estimate). Breadth: the estimate reads 13 reports (two averaging windows, the latest report, its employee counts) and the estimate/penalty history; the refund reads the account balance, the appeal credit, the late-penalty and interest history, the 2026-Q3 assessment and the cross-difficulty appeal record (outcome and filing date) set against the ledger's credited-back quarter payment. Negative space: the 2,000.00 paid toward 2026-Q2 is not a reason to skip the estimate (a payment is not a report), and it is absorbed by the estimate rather than refunded.

[Problem-tree card] root taxacct_ext_credit_refund_request <- taxacct_ext_estimated_assessment. Edge: kind value_input, gate credit_balance (also estimate_hold_factor), form state, prerequisite sentence (refund rule, affirmative "only after"): "The refundable amount is worked out only after the ledger carries an estimated assessment for every quarter whose report is still unfiled at least the class's estimated assessment days after its due date." Four-point test: (1) explicit ordering connective "only after" joining this policy's result (the refundable amount) to a waited-on state; the negated rewrite "is not worked out until the ledger carries ..." adds/drops nothing; the affirmative direction is how a refund desk states it ("worked out only after"), while task 1's relief sentence uses the negated direction ("is not fixed until"), so the charter carries both. (2) The waited-on side is a record-visible state (an estimated assessment entry on the ledger for each unfiled quarter past the estimate days), no action named. (3) No tool, policy id or code token. (4) Strength "only after"; scope "every quarter whose report is still unfiled at least the estimated assessment days after its due date" — exactly the condition field. Exactly one write of this difficulty brings that state about: the estimated assessment policy's own rule says an estimated assessment is booked for such a quarter, and its target tool is the only task tool that writes a contribution assessment with basis estimated_assessment (the penalty and relief tools of task 1 write a penalty and a request). Derivation: sentence + reports list (no 2026-Q2 report, due 2026-07-31, 132 days before 2026-12-10) + ledger (no 2026-Q2 assessment of any basis) + estimate rule -> book an estimated assessment for 2026-Q2. Seed evidence it is false at the opening: employer_wage_reports has no 2026-Q2 row; employer_tax_ledger's only 2026-Q2 rows are the 2,000.00 payment ACH-26073014870 and its reserve credit; account status delinquent. Topological order: estimate (step 7) then refund (step 9). Deletion sensitivity (actually run): skipping the estimate leaves requested_amount = 2726.36 instead of 325.00 (credit 3,076.50 instead of 769.44; estimate hold 1 instead of 0.5) and removes the estimate row from the terminal ledger. The customer's own write: the refund request (owner user) — asking for a refund is the employer's act under the blueprint; the agent unlocks and hands it over after computing the figure. user_scenario names neither problem id nor the estimate/missing report; tools validate nothing (each body is one ctx.create, plus one ctx.update of balance_due for the estimate).

[Factor card — estimate (expected 2307.06; whole baseline 1562.00)]
- estimate_wage_basis_rule (method, selection rule): ladder rising (latest >= 1.2 x recent average -> latest report) / fewer than 4 original reports within 12 months and not rising -> 24-month average / otherwise 12-month average (baseline). World: latest 2026-Q3 taxable 15,000.00 vs 1.2 x 78100.00; only 3 reports filed within 12 months (2025-Q4 on 2026-01-27, 2026-Q1 on 2026-04-27, 2026-Q3 on 2026-10-26; 2026-Q2 missing) -> basis = 24-month average 78471.4286 (7 reports, 549300.00). Baseline result 2296.14. Near-miss: 2025-Q3 (filed 2025-10-27) is 13 whole months back and falls outside the 12-month window but inside the 24-month one.
- estimate_history_uplift (parameter): 2+ estimates -> 2.0 / exactly one -> 1.5 / none -> class uplift 1.25. World: one estimate (2025-Q1, 2025-06-29, 17 months back) -> 1.5. Baseline 1977.48.
- late_filing_addon (parameter): 2+ late penalties -> +0.5 / one -> +0.25 / none -> 0. World: one penalty (2025-Q1, 2025-07-08) -> +0.25. Baseline 1977.48.
- workforce_growth_factor (parameter): third-month count >= 1.25 x first -> 1.10 / >= 1.10 x -> 1.05 / else 1. World: 2026-Q3 report 22 -> 25 (ratio 1.136) -> 1.05. Baseline 2197.2. Near-miss: ratio 1.136 is below 1.25, so the high tier must not be used.
Computation: 78471.4286 x (1.5 + 0.25) x 1.05 x 0.0160 = 2307.06.

[Factor card — refund (expected 325.00; whole baseline 769.44 = the credit after the estimate)]
- appeal_interest_allowance (method — it chooses the date the interest months are counted from; multi-source over two distinct records, the appeal row and the tax ledger; cross-difficulty: appeal): ladder (decided reversed or modified AND the credited-back quarter's last contribution payment on or after the appeal's filing date) -> interest from that payment's date / (decided reversed or modified AND that payment before the filing date) -> interest from the filing date / otherwise -> no allowance (baseline). The allowance is the class monthly interest rate (0.01) x the credited-back contributions x interest months (whole months to the request + 1). World (appeal product row seeded for this employer): decided reversed (mailed 2026-05-18), filed 2026-01-05; ledger: 1,076.50 credited back on 2026-Q1 (2026-05-26), whose last contribution payment is 2026-04-29 -> start 2026-04-29 -> 8 months -> 86.12. Near-miss: starting at the filing date would give 12 months (129.18). Baseline 286.25.
- reporting_cushion (parameter): late report penalties within the 8 abatement lookback quarters (24 months): 2+ -> 0.2 / one -> 0.1 / none -> 0. World: one (2025-07-08). Baseline 367.78.
- contribution_hold (parameter): late-payment interest entries within 12 months: 2+ -> 1.0 / one -> 0.5 / none -> 0 of the most recent original-report assessment. World: one (2026-02-28) -> 0.5 x 240.00. Near-miss: no interest arose on 2025-Q1. Baseline 385.0.
- estimate_hold (parameter, a factor value 0 / 0.5 / 1): estimates within 6 months: 2+ -> 0 / one -> 0.5 / none -> 1. World: the 2026-Q2 estimate just booked -> 0.5 (the 2025-Q1 estimate is 17 months back). Baseline 650.0.
Computation: max(0, (769.44 + 86.12) x 0.9 - 0.5 x 240.00) x 0.5 = 325.00.
Task-level floors: method factors = estimate_wage_basis_rule (estimate) and appeal_interest_allowance (refund); multi-source factor = appeal_interest_allowance (each non-fall-through tier joins a condition on the appeal row with a condition on a tax ledger payment row); cross-difficulty factor = appeal_interest_allowance (XLATEST value reads of the appeal product).

[Base-invariant card] Estimate write (subject taxacct_contribution_assessed): governed by taxacct_evt_quarterly_report, which has no gate applying to contribution assessments (its gates apply to wage_report_filed) -> policy_scope; its estimate sentence ("highest of the last four reported quarters' taxable wages times the uplift") is replaced by the extended estimate rule and declared in overwrite; the "replaced by the real figures when the report is filed" part is kept verbatim in the extended rule. Refund write (subject taxacct_refund_issued): governed by taxacct_evt_payments; gate refund_request_window (time): anchor = the payment that created the credit (employer_tax_ledger.entry_date of 33efc05b-dcd9-4050-a432-c34b8be46a27 = 2026-04-29), duration 36 calendar months (variants.credit_refund_request_months), counted from the payment date with month-end fall-back, inclusive, relation not_after; at 2026-12-10 the request is about 7 months in (satisfied); just-before/at-boundary cases: 2029-04-29 in time, 2029-04-30 late. The base clause "issued ... for no more than the credit balance" is replaced (declared) because the appeal interest allowance may lift the figure above the credit. Lineage completeness: no other base policy has refund_issued or contribution_assessed in its subject.

[Business-object card] Target account f19d862d-6cba-49b5-8123-21b320428bb3 (single open account of the employer). Estimate object: quarter 2026-Q2 (the only quarter without a report). Refund object: the credit balance after the estimate, 769.44, created by the 2026-05-26 appeal re-assessment of the 2026-Q1 contributions paid by ACH debit on 2026-04-29 (entry 33efc05b-dcd9-4050-a432-c34b8be46a27); the 2,000.00 paid toward 2026-Q2 is fully absorbed by the 2026-Q2 estimate (2307.06), so it is not the credit's source after the estimate. Rows excluded: settled quarters (payments equal assessments), the 2025-Q1 replacement assessment (an original_report row older than the 2026-Q3 assessment, so not the latest), the 2025-Q1 interest that never arose.

[World rows and why] 13 original reports 2023-Q2..2026-Q3 (2026-Q2 missing; 2025-Q1 filed 2025-06-30, one day after a 60-day estimate) — feed both averages, the latest report, its counts, and the missing-quarter fact; taxable wages follow the 14,000 per-employee annual base (Q1 large, Q3/Q4 small). Ledger (47 rows): contributions assessed at the rate in force (0.0270 for 2023–2025; 2026-Q1 at the original 2026 notice rate 0.0210; 2026-Q3 at the revised 0.0160), payments and same-day reserve credits, the 2025-Q1 estimate 2,863.93 (computed with this charter's estimate rule on the records of 2025-06-29: 24-month average 84,857.14 x 1.25 x 1 x 0.0270) and its replacement 2,617.07, the 2025-Q1 late report penalty 519.00 (computed with task 1's penalty rule on 2025-07-08: 61 days late -> 0.002 x 222,000 = 444.00, no repeat, cap 500, estimate charge 75.00), its payment, the February 2026 interest 1.08 and its payment, the appeal credit 1,076.50, the 2026-Q2 payment 2,000.00. Account: delinquent (2026-Q2 report missing), rate 0.0160 / ratio 0.0725 on the revised notice of 2026-05-21; ratio = 21,519.00 credited by 2025-06-30 / 297,000.00 average payroll of fiscal years 2023–2025; the original notice had left out the 5,481.00 paid on the computation date itself (ratio 0.0540, rate 0.0210) — the appeal reversed that. Appeal row (appeal product, read-only): reversed, closed 2026-06-18 when the Board of Review deadline passed. Automatic clauses checked: delinquency already flagged; no interest is due for 2026-Q2 at the opening (nothing assessed for it); the estimate will start interest from its month end, which is the monthly interest run's job, not an agent write; no report, penalty or cure is owed at the opening other than the estimate.

[Persona design] Marisol Ibsen-Achterberg, controller, brisk and organized. Volunteers only: the appeal was won in May, a credit shows online, she wants it refunded and to request it today, she is authorized. Locator/verification only when asked (phone 6085554118, FEIN last four 4462, ZIP 53764; email as a spare). The 2026-Q2 payment and the missing report surface only if the agent asks about that quarter; she cannot file it today and accepts the Department's booking. Passive reactions: consent to booking first; one question about why the figure is lower than the credit (answered by the refund rule, no write); submits the refund request herself with the agent's details; ends on "received". She never gives a figure, never corrects one, never mentions an estimate.

[Reachability walk-through] (0) find_customers by phone -> profile; (1) verify with three details; (2) account; (3) reports (missing 2026-Q2 visible); (4) ledger (estimate/penalty/interest/appeal-credit/payment history; payment entry 33efc05b-dcd9-4050-a432-c34b8be46a27); (5) appeals by customer (outcome, dates); (6–7) unlock + book estimate 2307.06 for 2026-Q2; (8–9) unlock user tool, the caller lodges the refund request for 325.00 citing 33efc05b-dcd9-4050-a432-c34b8be46a27; her receipt (request reference) comes back through the shared transcript. Everything runs at one frozen_time; no waiting on filing, clearing or review is required for any write (the refund payout itself happens later and is not part of the tree).

[Easiest mistakes] refunding the 3,076.50 credit as shown (ignoring the unfiled quarter) -> 2726.36-type figures; using the 12-month average (78,100.00) instead of the 24-month one; using the class uplift 1.25; forgetting the add-on; applying the cushion after the hold; citing the 2026-Q2 payment as the credit's source.

[Verification code and outputs] /tmp generator (removed from the write domain) replays gold writes with the real tools and evaluates each policy with check_compute's own evaluator: estimate = 2307.06 (factor baselines {'estimate_wage_basis_rule': 2296.14, 'estimate_history_uplift': 1977.48, 'late_filing_addon': 1977.48, 'workforce_growth_factor': 2197.2}; all-baseline 1562.0); after the estimate the balance is -769.44; refund = 325.00 (factor baselines {'appeal_interest_allowance': 286.25, 'reporting_cushion': 367.78, 'contribution_hold': 385.0, 'estimate_hold': 650.0}; all-baseline 769.44); refund with the estimate skipped = 2726.36. Gates run per task: check_task_tools, check_extended --task 0, replay_tasks --task 0, check_solvability --task 0, check_compute --task 0, check_grounding --task 0, check_cross_fire --task 0 (outputs recorded in the final report).

[Closure] policy -> tool -> computation -> GT call -> terminal state: taxacct_ext_estimated_assessment -> book_estimated_assessment_54fbfb5a -> computations[0] (step 7, assessment_amount) -> new 2026-Q2 estimated assessment row + balance_due -769.44; taxacct_ext_credit_refund_request -> request_credit_refund_f44db5b5 -> computations[1] (step 9, requested_amount) -> new employer_account_requests row (credit_refund, received). required_documents = charter_scope.extended_policies. No handoff in gold.

[Draft recomputation from the visible context] Reading only the two rules, the tool docstrings, the five lookups and the persona: the refund rule's prerequisite sentence sends the agent to the reports, which lack 2026-Q2; the estimate rule (fewer than four reports in 12 months, not rising -> 24-month average; one prior estimate -> 1.5; one penalty -> +0.25; 25/22 -> 1.05; rate 0.0160) gives 2307.06; the refund rule on the updated balance (interest from the 2026-04-29 payment, 8 months) gives 325.00; the payment cited is the 2026-04-29 entry, as the refund rule now states. Matches gold.


[Round 2 rework — audit audits/policy_task/employer_quarterly_contributions (_difficulty.md, 0.md)] T0-F1 / F-1: estimate_hold relabelled parameter (values 0 / 0.5 / 1); appeal_interest_allowance rebuilt as an honest method factor that chooses the interest start date (payment date / appeal filing date / none) with the class monthly interest rate x months, so the refund keeps 3 parameter + 1 method. T0-F2 / F-4: that factor's non-fall-through tiers each join the appeal row (outcome, filing date) with a tax ledger payment row (the credited-back quarter's last contribution payment) — distinct records. O-1: the prerequisite sentence and the estimate trigger both say "at least the class's estimated assessment days after its due date". O-3: the appeal is read as the most recently decided contribution-rate appeal (XLATEST by decision mailing date) and the contribution hold rule now says "the most recent contribution assessment booked from an original report". T0-O1: the rule now states which payment the request cites. Recomputed: refund 325.00 (was 293.52), skip-prerequisite 2726.36 (was 2663.39), factor baselines {'appeal_interest_allowance': 286.25, 'reporting_cushion': 367.78, 'contribution_hold': 385.0, 'estimate_hold': 650.0}; estimate unchanged at 2307.06.

[Round 3 rework — audit revision_2 observations] R2-O3: the appeal interest allowance is now worked out on the contributions credited back within the appeal credit months to the quarter most recently credited back on appeal (the credited-back quarter), so the credited amount and the payment date read the same quarter; the no-allowance case no longer uses the request day as a sentinel (an empty start date, so a payment dated the request day would count one month). R2-O2: the contribution-hold basis quote now matches the rule. On this world exactly one quarter (2026-Q1) is credited back and no payment is dated 2026-12-10, so every figure is unchanged: refund 325.00, factor baselines {'appeal_interest_allowance': 286.25, 'reporting_cushion': 367.78, 'contribution_hold': 385.0, 'estimate_hold': 650.0}, all-baseline 769.44, skip-estimate 2726.36; estimate 2307.06.
user_scenario: You are Marisol Ibsen-Achterberg, the controller of Halvorsen-Okafor Precision Tooling, Inc., a 25-person machine shop in Brantwood. You are calling the Lakeland Department of Workforce Security on a Thursday morning between month-end tasks, organized and brisk but polite. You open by explaining that your company won its contribution rate appeal back in May and that ever since, the online account has shown a credit sitting there; you want that credit paid back to the company as a refund rather than left on the books, and you would like to get the refund request in today on this call. You are the person who handles the company's unemployment tax account and you are authorized to act for it. When the agent asks you to identify the account, you give the company name and the phone number 6085554118; when asked to verify, you give the last four digits of the company's federal employer identification number, 4462, and the ZIP code of the mailing address, 53764, and if a further detail is wanted you give the email address of record, payroll@halvorsenokaforprecisiontooling.com. You do not have the state account number or any internal reference numbers to hand, and you say the agent will have to look those up. You do not volunteer anything about other quarters. Only if the agent asks about the second quarter of 2026 or about a missing report do you say that your former bookkeeper sent two thousand dollars toward that quarter at the end of July and that you assumed the report went in with it; you cannot file that report today because the payroll register for the spring quarter is with your outside accountant, and you accept that the Department will record whatever it has to on its side in the meantime without arguing about it. If the agent tells you that something has to be booked on the account before the refund figure can be worked out, you say that is fine and that they should go ahead. If the agent explains that the amount that can be asked for now is less than the credit you see, or that part of it has to stay on the account, you ask once, in a sentence, what the main reason is, accept the explanation without disputing the arithmetic, and say you would still like to request whatever can go out now. You do not know any of the figures yourself beyond the two thousand dollar payment, you never suggest an amount, and you never correct the agent's numbers. Once the agent hands you the refund request to submit, you submit it yourself with exactly the details the agent gives you, and when you see that the request has been received you thank the agent, confirm you have what you need, and end the call.

base_preconditions.condition: A refund of a credit balance is issued only when it is requested no later than the refund limit after the payment that created the credit.

temporal_feasibility.condition: A refund of a credit balance is issued only when it is requested no later than the refund limit after the payment that created the credit.

temporal_basis.anchor_event: the payment that created the credit
temporal_basis.counting_rule: The limit is counted in calendar months from the payment date, a month-end payment date falling back to the last day of a shorter month, and a request on the last day is in time.

boundary_check.just_before: The credit-creating payment was received 2026-04-29; the refund limit of 36 calendar months runs to 2029-04-29. A request on 2026-12-10 is about 7 months in, well inside the limit.
boundary_check.at_boundary: A request on 2029-04-29 (the last day, inclusive) would still be in time; a request on 2029-04-30 would be too late and no refund could be issued.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Verify the caller against the profile with three matching details (phone, FEIN last four, ZIP).
evaluation_criteria.necessity: No tax account information may be discussed or changed before the caller is verified.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the tax account: class, status (delinquent), balance due (a credit of 3,076.50), contribution rate 0.0160 for rate year 2026.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The refund baseline is the credit shown in balance_due; the estimate multiplies by the contribution rate on the account; the delinquent status points to an unfiled report.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read every quarterly report: quarters, due and filing dates, taxable wages, employee counts; notice that 2026-Q2 has no report although its due date passed on 2026-07-31.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the balance and reserve history: the 2025-Q1 estimated assessment and late report penalty, the February 2026 interest entry, the 2026-Q1 appeal credit, the 2,000.00 payment for 2026-Q2 and the 2026-Q3 assessment.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Supplies the estimate uplift and late filing add-on evidence, the refund cushion, contribution hold, estimate hold and the contributions credited back to the credited-back quarter, and that quarter's last contribution payment, which both starts the appeal interest and is the payment the request cites.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.employer_account_id: (1) f19d862d-6cba-49b5-8123-21b320428bb3. (2) Basis: the employer account lookup returns the single account of this employer; the tool docstring asks for 'the reference number of the employer's unemployment insurance tax account, as returned by the employer account lookup'. (3) Uniqueness: the employer holds one open account (taxacct_agg_multi_holding), so every correct agent passes the same reference.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.quarter: (1) 2026-Q2. (2) Basis: the estimated assessment rule 'An estimated assessment is booked for a quarter whose quarterly contribution and wage report is still unfiled the class's estimated assessment days after its due date'; the wage report lookup shows reports for 2026-Q1 (filed 2026-04-27) and 2026-Q3 (filed 2026-10-26) but none for 2026-Q2, whose due date 2026-07-31 is 132 days before 2026-12-10 (more than the class's 60 estimated assessment days). (3) Uniqueness: every other quarter of the account has an original report, so 2026-Q2 is the only quarter the rule selects; the docstring fixes the YYYY-Qn format.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.assessment_amount: (1) 2307.06. (2) Factors: wage basis method — the latest report (2026-Q3) shows 15000.00 taxable wages, below the rising wage ratio 1.2 x the recent average 78100.00, and only 3 original reports were filed within the recent 12 months (fewer than a year's 4 quarters), so the basis is the 24-month average 78471.4286 (549300.00 over 7 reports) instead of the recent average; uplift — one estimated assessment (2025-Q1, 2025-06-29) within 24 months gives the one-estimate uplift 1.5 instead of the class uplift 1.25; late filing add-on — one late report penalty (2025-Q1, 2025-07-08) within 24 months adds 0.25; growth factor — the 2026-Q3 report's third-month count 25 is at least 1.1 x and below 1.25 x its first-month count 22, giving 1.05; rate on the account 0.0160. Product: 78471.4286 x (1.5 + 0.25) x 1.05 x 0.0160 = 2307.06, rounded once at the end. (3) The record set is fixed, so every agent applying the rule reaches the same figure; omitting any factor gives a different figure (see factor_sensitivity).

evaluation_criteria.objective: Unlock the employer's refund request tool so the caller can lodge the request herself.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Asking for a refund is the employer's own act; the agent unlocks and hands it over.

evaluation_criteria.necessity: taxacct_ext_credit_refund_request computes requested_amount on the account as it stands after the estimate is booked.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.employer_account_id: (1) f19d862d-6cba-49b5-8123-21b320428bb3. (2) Basis: the same account returned by the employer account lookup; the docstring asks for the account reference as returned by that lookup. (3) Uniqueness: one open account.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.credit_payment_entry_id: (1) 33efc05b-dcd9-4050-a432-c34b8be46a27. (2) Basis: the refund rule 'The request cites the payment that created the credit: where the credit arose from contributions credited back to a quarter, it is the last contribution payment received for that quarter.' After the 2026-Q2 estimate (2307.06) absorbs the 2,000.00 paid toward 2026-Q2 (a payment designated for a quarter is applied to that quarter), the remaining credit of 769.44 is part of the 1,076.50 credited back on 2026-05-26 (rate reduced on appeal) on 2026-Q1, whose last contribution payment is the ACH debit entry of 2026-04-29 (ACH-26042913385). (3) Uniqueness: 2026-Q1 has one contribution payment; the credit adjustment entry is not a payment; the 2026-Q2 payment funds no credit once the estimate is booked.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.requested_amount: (1) 325.00. (2) Factors: credit balance 769.44 after the estimate; appeal interest allowance (method, interest start date) — the most recently decided contribution rate appeal was decided reversed and the credited-back quarter 2026-Q1's last contribution payment (2026-04-29) was received on or after the appeal's filing date (2026-01-05), so interest runs from the payment date: whole months to 2026-12-10 = 7, plus one for the month in progress = 8; 1,076.50 x the class monthly rate 0.01 x 8 = 86.12; reporting cushion — one late report penalty within the 8 abatement lookback quarters keeps back 0.1; contribution hold — one late payment interest entry (2026-02-28) within 12 months holds 0.5 of the most recent original-report assessment 240.00; estimate hold — exactly one estimated assessment (the one just booked) within 6 months gives 0.5. ((769.44 + 86.12) x (1 - 0.1) - 0.5 x 240.00) x 0.5 = 325.002 -> 325.00, rounded once at the end. (3) Every factor rests on fixed records; the figure is unique.

factor_trace: estimate_wage_basis_rule (method): evidence: latest original report 2026-Q3 taxable 15000.00 < 1.2 x recent average 78100.00; 3 original reports filed within 12 months (< 4) -> tier 'longer average'; basis 78471.4286 (24-month sum 549300.00 / 7); standard method would use the recent average 78100.00. Baseline reading gives result 2296.14.

estimate_history_uplift (parameter): evidence: 1 estimated assessment within 24 months (2025-Q1 estimate of 2025-06-29) -> tier 'exactly one' -> 1.5; standard uplift 1.25. Baseline reading gives result 1977.48.

late_filing_addon (parameter): evidence: 1 late report penalty within 24 months (2025-Q1 penalty of 2025-07-08) -> tier 'exactly one' -> 0.25; standard adds nothing. Baseline reading gives result 1977.48.
workforce_growth_factor (parameter): evidence: 2026-Q3 report counts first month 22, third month 25 (ratio 1.1364) -> tier 'mid growth' -> 1.05; standard 1. Baseline reading gives result 2197.2.

Non-factor bindings: recent_report_wages 234300.00 / recent_report_count 3 -> recent_average 78100.00; contribution rate on the account F(contribution_rate) = 0.0160; result = basis x (uplift + add-on) x growth x rate = 2307.06.

factor_sensitivity.tier_taken: fewer original reports than a year's quarters within the recent report months, rising test not met: longer report average
exactly one estimated assessment within the estimate history months
exactly one late report penalty within the estimate history months
third-month count at least the mid growth ratio but below the high growth ratio times the first-month count

factor_trace: appeal_interest_allowance (method: chooses the interest start date; multi-source over the appeal record and the tax ledger; cross-difficulty appeal): evidence — appeal product: Lower Authority Appeal — Employer Contribution Rate, decided reversed (decision mailed 2026-05-18), filed 2026-01-05; tax ledger: credit_adjusted rate_reduced_on_appeal on 2026-Q1 (1,076.50, 2026-05-26), that quarter's last contribution payment 2026-04-29 (on or after the filing date) -> interest starts on the payment date -> 8 interest months -> allowance 86.12; the standard method adds no allowance. Baseline reading gives result 286.25.
reporting_cushion (parameter): evidence: 1 late report penalty within 24 months (2025-07-08) -> 0.1 kept back; standard keeps back nothing. Baseline reading gives result 367.78.

contribution_hold (parameter): evidence: 1 interest entry within 12 months (2026-02-28) -> 0.5 of the most recent original-report assessment 240.00; standard holds nothing. Baseline reading gives result 385.0.
estimate_hold (parameter): evidence: 1 estimated assessment within 6 months (the 2026-Q2 estimate booked at step 7) -> 0.5; standard 1. Baseline reading gives result 650.0.

Non-factor bindings: credit_balance = max(0, -balance_due) = 769.44 on the handling-time world (balance due -769.44 after the estimate); interest_months = whole months from the start date to the request + 1 = 8; appeal_interest = RND(1076.50 x P(late_payment_interest_rate_monthly) 0.01 x 8) = 86.12; result = max(0, (credit + allowance) x (1 - cushion) - hold share x 240.00) x estimate hold = 325.00.

factor_sensitivity.tier_taken: the appeal was decided as reversed or modified AND the credited-back quarter's last contribution payment was received on or after the appeal's filing date
exactly one late report penalty within the abatement lookback
exactly one late payment interest entry within the payment record months
exactly one estimated assessment within the estimate hold months

edges.condition: Every quarter of the account whose report is still unfiled at least the estimated assessment days after its due date carries an estimated contribution assessment entry on the employer tax ledger.
edges.policy_source: The refundable amount is worked out only after the ledger carries an estimated assessment for every quarter whose report is still unfiled at least the class's estimated assessment days after its due date.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: Quarter 2026-Q2 has no quarterly report on the account (the reports cover 2023-Q2 to 2026-Q1 and 2026-Q3), its due date 2026-07-31 is 132 calendar days before 2026-12-10 — at least the 60 estimated assessment days — and the ledger carries no estimated assessment for 2026-Q2: its only 2026-Q2 entries are the 2,000.00 payment and its reserve credit. The account is delinquent for that missing report.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The estimated assessment written at step 7 adds a taxacct_contribution_assessed entry for 2026-Q2 with assessment_basis estimated_assessment and amount 2307.06; balance_due moves from -3076.50 to -769.44, so credit_balance becomes 769.44 and the estimate hold counts one estimate.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: A single edge: the refund (root) depends on the estimate. The estimate reads only reports and ledger history that the refund request never writes (the request writes only an employer_account_requests row), so the estimate value is the same whenever it is booked; the refund, by contrast, reads balance_due and the estimated-assessment count, which the estimate changes. The prerequisite sentence fixes the order: the refundable amount is worked out only after the ledger carries the estimate.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the estimate leaves balance_due at -3076.50 (credit_balance 3076.50) and no recent estimate (estimate hold 1), so requested_amount would be 2726.36 instead of 325.00; the terminal ledger would also lack the 2026-Q2 estimated assessment row of 2307.06 and the account balance would differ.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: The persona asks only for the credit to be refunded. It never mentions an estimated assessment, a missing report or anything that must be booked first; the second-quarter payment is disclosed only if the agent asks about 2026-Q2 or a missing report, and the persona says nothing about what the Department should do with it beyond accepting it.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: request_credit_refund_f44db5b5 creates the employer_account_requests row with whatever requested_amount it is given and never reads the ledger, the reports or any estimate; book_estimated_assessment_54fbfb5a books the assessment with the amount given and checks no report status. Neither returns an error when a prerequisite is unmet (see the two function bodies in task_tools.py: one ctx.create plus, for the estimate, one ctx.update of balance_due).
